prompt:
Three blocks A, B, and C of masses 2.0 kg, 3.0 kg, and 5.0 kg respectively are placed in contact in a straight line on a rough horizontal surface. A horizontal force P = 55 N pushes block A to the right. Constant frictional forces of 3.0 N on block A, 4.5 N on block B, and 7.5 N on block C oppose the motion.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram showing three blocks A (2.0 kg), B (3.0 kg), and C (5.0 kg) in contact on a horizontal surface. A horizontal force P = 55 N pushes block A to the right. Opposing frictional forces of 3.0 N, 4.5 N, and 7.5 N act on blocks A, B, and C respectively.]
(a) Show that the acceleration of the blocks is 4.0 m s^-2. [2]
(b) Calculate the resultant force acting on block B alone. [1]
(c) Calculate the magnitude of the contact force exerted by block A on block B. [2]
(d) Calculate the magnitude of the contact force exerted by block B on block C. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Calculates total mass = 10.0 kg and total friction = 15.0 N, giving net force = 55 - 15.0 = 40.0 N.
Resultant force on B = m_B * a = 3.0 * 4.0 = 12 N.
Sets up force equation for block A: 55 - 3.0 - F_AB = m_A * a = 2.0 * 4.0 = 8.0 N.
Sets up equation for block C: F_BC - 7.5 = 5.0 * 4.0 = 20.0 N, giving F_BC = 27.5 N.

marking_points.criterion: Calculates total mass = 10.0 kg and total friction = 15.0 N to give resultant force = 40.0 N.

part_enrichment.guidance: Sum all masses (2.0 + 3.0 + 5.0 = 10.0 kg) and all resistances (3.0 + 4.5 + 7.5 = 15.0 N). Subtract total resistance from applied push P = 55 N.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Forgetting to sum the individual frictional forces across all three blocks.

marking_points.criterion: Calculates resultant force on B alone: F_res = 3.0 * 4.0 = 12 N.

part_enrichment.guidance: By Newton's second law, resultant force on any individual body equals its mass multiplied by system acceleration.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Confusing the resultant force on B with the contact force exerted by A on B.

marking_points.criterion: Formulates equation of motion for block A: P - Friction_A - F_AB = m_A * a.
Solves for contact force F_AB = 44 N.

part_enrichment.guidance: Block A experiences forward push 55 N, backward friction 3.0 N, and backward contact force from B. 55 - 3.0 - F_AB = 2.0 * 4.0.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Assuming the contact force between A and B equals the applied push P.

marking_points.criterion: Calculates contact force F_BC = m_C * a + Friction_C = 20.0 + 7.5 = 27.5 N.

part_enrichment.guidance: Isolate block C: forward force is F_BC, opposing friction is 7.5 N. F_BC - 7.5 = 5.0 * 4.0 = 20.0 N.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Subtracting friction instead of adding it when rearranging for forward contact force.

hints: In part (a), find total mass and total opposing friction for the whole three-block system.
In part (b), resultant force on block B is simply m_B * a.
In part (c), apply Newton's second law to block A alone to find the internal contact force between A and B.
In part (d), apply Newton's second law to block C alone.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Emphasize whole-system analysis. Internal contact forces cancel out when considering all three blocks together. Resultant force = 55 - 15 = 40 N, a = 40 / 10 = 4.0 m s^-2.
Part (b): Resultant force on B alone is simply m_B * a = 3.0 * 4.0 = 12 N.
Part (c): Free-body diagram for block A: 55 N right, 3.0 N left (friction), F_AB left (contact from B). Resultant force is 52 - F_AB = 2.0 * 4.0 = 8.0 N => F_AB = 44 N.

Part (d): Free-body diagram for block C: F_BC right (contact from B), 7.5 N left (friction). F_BC - 7.5 = 5.0 * 4.0 = 20.0 N => F_BC = 27.5 N. Verify on block B: F_AB - F_BC - friction_B = 44 - 27.5 - 4.5 = 12 N, which matches part (b) perfectly.
